gloss: to go off on a tangent; to digress; to stray from the main road

definitions.gloss: to veer off the main road onto a side road; to stray off the main path
definitions.explanation: Literal sense. To leave the main road and move onto a smaller, branching road. Used of cars, walkers, animals, and so on. The literal sense is less common in everyday conversation than the figurative one but still shows up in driving directions, travel writing, and descriptions of a landscape.

definitions.gloss: to go off on a tangent; to digress from the main topic of a conversation, lecture, or piece of writing
definitions.explanation: Figurative sense, by far the more common one. To drift away from the main topic of what one is saying or writing. Often used self-deprecatingly — the speaker or writer notices they have wandered off course and wants to bring the discussion back. The image is clearly that of a traveler accidentally turning onto a side street instead of continuing along the main road.

examples.japanese: ⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれた。
examples.english: The car turned off onto a side road.

examples.japanese: {国道|こくどう}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれる⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧な⟦{田舎|いなか}→田舎：01320_inaka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風景|ふうけい}→風景：03591_fuukei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{広|ひろ}がっていた→広がる：01980_hirogaru⟧。
examples.english: When we turned off the main highway onto a side road, quiet countryside scenery spread out before us.

examples.japanese: ⟦{近道|ちかみち}→近道：03118_chikamichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦つもり→つもり：01152_tsumori⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれたら、かえって⟦{遠回|とおまわ}り→遠回り：14380_toomawari⟧になってしまった。
examples.english: I took a side road thinking it would be a shortcut, but it ended up being a detour instead.

examples.japanese: ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれた。
examples.english: The conversation went off on a tangent.

examples.japanese: すみません、⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれてしまいました。
examples.english: Sorry, I've gone off on a tangent.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれる⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{雑談|ざつだん}→雑談：06639_zatsudan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧⟦{面白|おもしろ}い→面白い：00589_omoshiroi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧たち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{評判|ひょうばん}→評判：03586_hyouban⟧だ。
examples.english: The teacher's lectures often wander off on tangents, but the students say those digressions are the most interesting part.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{脇道|わきみち}→脇道：13943_wakimichi⟧ (side road, side path) + ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (target particle) + ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧る (to stray, to veer off course). The verb ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧る is usually written ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧る in hiragana, though ⟦{逸|そ}れる→逸れる：17195_soreru⟧ is the kanji form. A very common figurative expression built on the transparent image of leaving the main road.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれる: the conversation goes off on a tangent
- ⟦{議論|ぎろん}→議論：02650_giron⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれる: the discussion goes off-topic
- ⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれる: the topic drifts off course
- {脇道|わきみち}にそれてしまう: to end up going off on a tangent (with a note of self-awareness)
- ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{本筋|ほんすじ}→本筋：21085_honsuji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{戻|もど}す→戻す：02317_modosu⟧: to bring the conversation back to the main point (the typical "rescue" phrase after a tangent)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{逸|そ}れる→逸れる：17195_soreru⟧: the conversation strays off — a plainer near-synonym, without the "side road" metaphor.
- ⟦{本題|ほんだい}→本題：12877_hondai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{外|はず}れる→外れる：02395_hazureru⟧: to stray from the main topic — a slightly more formal alternative.
- {横道|よこみち}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧それる: to go off onto a side road / tangent — essentially interchangeable with {脇道|わきみち}にそれる.
- ⟦{脱線|だっせん}→脱線：04514_dassen⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: (literally "to derail") to go wildly off-topic — stronger and more vivid, often used of lectures or speeches.

USAGE:
The figurative sense 2 is so common that when a speaker or writer uses this phrase out of context, listeners usually assume they mean a conversational digression. The literal sense of turning onto a side street is still understood but is more common in travel writing and driving directions.

Self-correction in conversation often takes the form ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{脇道|わきみち}にそれてしまいました⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{本題|ほんだい}→本題：12877_hondai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{戻|もど}ります→戻る：01117_modoru⟧ ("I've gone off on a tangent, but let me return to the main topic"). This is a polite and very common pattern in presentations and meetings.

REGISTER:
Neutral. Used freely in both spoken and written Japanese, from casual conversation to formal lectures.
